about.title: Reedley Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Reedley's economy runs on agriculture, packing houses, and the trucking and warehouse work that moves produce along Manning Avenue and I Street corridors. That mix means workplace injuries here often involve heavy equipment, forklifts, ladders, or delivery vehicles rather than a typical office mishap. Under California law, workers' compensation usually pays medical bills and partial wage replacement regardless of fault, but it doesn't account for full pain and suffering. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge fees; we simply connect injured Reedley workers with an independent attorney who can look at both angles of a claim and explain what timelines and options actually apply to your situation, so you're not left guessing while you're trying to recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Reedley Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Two Paths, One Conversation
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, many injured workers never realize a negligent third party might owe them a separate claim. An independent attorney can review both possibilities at once.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires you to notify your employer of a workplace injury within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your benefits. Getting guidance early helps make sure your report is filed correctly.

items.title: Retaliation Isn't Legal
items.desc: You're protected from employer retaliation for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job while dealing with an injury, that's a conversation worth having with an attorney.

items.question: I was hurt at a Reedley packing house — can I still file a separate injury claim?
items.answer: Workers' comp is typically the only claim available against your employer directly, but if equipment failure, a subcontractor, or another company's negligence played a role, a third-party claim may be possible. An independent attorney can review the details of your incident to see which paths apply. There's no cost to have that conversation through LawProactive.

items.question: How long do I have to act after a workplace injury in Fresno County?
items.answer: You generally need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' comp benefits. If a third-party claim is involved, California law gives you two years from the date of injury to file that separate lawsuit. Waiting too long can limit your options, so earlier guidance tends to help.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you notice reduced hours, demotion, or termination tied to your report, an independent attorney can advise you on next steps. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles these situations.
